chapter_note: Dominant old teaching layer: a systematic pentadic/decadic cosmology of Death’s five elements and five worlds, doubling into male/female to yield twelve parts, then correlated with zodiacal signs. Late hagiographic frame appears in ¶1 and a doxological close in ¶10. The main editorial graft is ¶8–¶9, where the cosmic scheme is explicitly applied to the “holy church” and contemporary “sects,” i.e., cosmos → present institution/polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: Did Death arise and stand firm [...] up? Or else did it turn itself from [...] its armour [...] in its [...] but it finished [...] the two [...].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic sitting-scene and dialogue frame: “Once again, the enlightener is sitting in the midst of his disciples…” and “His disciples say to him […]:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear frame markers (“Once again…”, disciples in attendance) introduce a substantive cosmological question about Death’s arising within the two essences; the question itself likely preserves the older inquiry-topic.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.48⟩ [...] it moved it and [...] they that are in the [...] of the earth of Darkness [...] first part.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extremely lacunose, but what remains stays inside the cosmic geography (“earth of Darkness,” “first part”) with no institutional or citation language; tentatively treated as core continuation.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, after a long time, as there was not [...], it gushed and streamed up [...] the five elements of Death that gushed [...] which are smoke, fire, wind, water and Darkness [...] the second time [...] they were sculpted [...] those in which Death was established [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological enumeration (five elements named) in an impersonal explanatory voice; this is classic substrate-style degree teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth part is the evil fruits [...] in the five trees that are in the five worlds of the land of Darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential mapping internal to the dark cosmos (fruits/trees/worlds) with pentadic structure; no contemporary referents.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth time it spread itself out to its creatures that exist in the five worlds; the ones that were formed and generated from the five fruits of Death. They are the five worlds of flesh, the five creations of Darkness in which Death has been established. It spread itself out to ten parts, five male parts and five female [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pentad → decad (male/female doubling) is structural cosmology, not exhortation; remains wholly within the system of Darkness/Death.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, like the land of Darkness, in that its spirit and its [...] they nourished the five elements [...]; this is also [how] the ten parts that are in male and female, the Fire and Lust of the flesh [...] them, as they yoke them with one another [...] they were established against the First Man. This is [...] of the Darkness, it was condemned for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanistic explanation of how the doubled parts plus Fire/Lust operate against the First Man—cosmos → cosmos causality, no institutional pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: Alongside the mystery of these twelve parts that came about in the Darkness [...] against the First Man. The twelve [...] the twelve spirits of error that came about from the twelve signs of the zodiac [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Twelvefold correlation (parts/spirits/zodiac) is a closed correspondential system. “Spirits of error” could be later polemical colouring, but here it still functions as an internal cosmic taxonomy tied to the zodiac.
Explicit cosmos→institution graft: the mythic pursuit is transferred to “the second living man, who dwells in the holy church,” anchoring the scheme in the editor’s ecclesial present.
Continues the application into the contemporary world (“light that dwells in the church,” “the twelve sects”); this is polemical/institutional use of the scheme rather than core cosmology.
Doxological closure formula (“for ever and ever”) belongs to the compiling community’s liturgical/hagiographic apparatus, not the teaching substrate.
